extracted.intended_audience: sketch comedy writers and performers studying Tim Robinson's alt/cringe style
extracted.subtask_description: Craft short sketch comedy in the Tim Robinson / alt-cringe mode: center a clearly-wrong character in a hyper-specific, mundane situation and escalate by having them refuse to admit error until the scene spirals into surreal, humiliating chaos.

rubrics_metrics.name: A character who is gloriously, spectacularly wrong
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sketch revolves around: a character who is gloriously, spectacularly wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The character's incorrectness should be central and driving: they are the engine of the joke rather than a passive observer. Examples: 'Driving Crooner', 'Hot Dog Suit'. Anti-pattern: a diffuse or ensemble-focused premise where no single character embodies the error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuses to budge / refuses to admit they're wrong
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuses to budge, lest they be humiliated by admitting wrong. Do they refuse to admit it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the character's denial as a psychological motive (fear of humiliation). Denial must persist through escalating evidence. Anti-patterns: characters who quickly concede, apologize, or wink to the audience; premature confession deflates the crank-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doubles down rather than relenting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When challenged, the character escalates their position or behavior instead of backing down — this multiplication of commitment escalates stakes and absurdity. Use believable but increasingly extreme attempts to 'prove' their point. Anti-pattern: a single, flat response that doesn't increase the tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation spirals into chaos via doubling-down
rubrics_metrics.description: Character spirals into chaos; does the situation spiral via doubling-down?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the scene so each refusal/doubling-down compounds consequences and widens the disaster. The spiral should feel causally linked to the character's actions (not random). Anti-pattern: disconnected gags that don't build cumulatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyper-specific writing / hyper-specific scenarios
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrowly detailed, concrete specifics (objects, lines, settings) that make the premise feel vividly real and therefore funnier when it collapses. Specificity helps the audience recognize and identify with the situation. Anti-pattern: vague, generic descriptions that fail to anchor the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mundane everyday scenarios as the setup
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from ordinary, relatable situations (office meeting, contest, car ride) so the escalation feels grounded and surprising. The contrast between mundane setup and escalating absurdity produces cringe. Anti-pattern: starting in an already surreal world with no relatable anchor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience cringes with recognition ('we've all been THAT person')
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the audience cringe with recognition? The humor comes from recognition — we've all been THAT person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for moments of painful identification: small truths about social anxiety, pride, or denial that cause empathetic cringe. Avoid inventing idiosyncrasies so bizarre that viewers can't recognize themselves in the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum commitment to character / tonal commitment without winking
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum commitment to character; tonal commitment without winking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors must fully inhabit the character (no parody or meta-telling). The show must not wink at the audience or undercut the situation with knowing asides; tonal seriousness amplifies the awkwardness. Anti-pattern: performers who break character or signal 'it's a joke' through tone or expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exit ramp from cringe
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid giving the character or scene an easy out (apology, reveal it was staged, corrective punchline). The scene should sustain discomfort until the escalation reaches its peak. Anti-pattern: providing relief too early or a tidy resolution that neutralizes the cringe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awkwardness as the engine / neurodivergent feel
rubrics_metrics.description: Awkwardness as engine; 'Comedy of autism' / neurodivergent feel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let social awkwardness, misreading, and perseverative behavior drive the humor. Note: this tonal description can be sensitive — avoid mocking or stereotyping real disabilities; use awkwardness to explore universal social pain rather than to demean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surreal flourishes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce increasingly absurd, surreal elements as the scene escalates (imagery, actions, rules bending). Surreal touches should grow naturally from the character's doubling-down rather than feeling tacked-on. Anti-pattern: abrupt surrealism that breaks the scene's internal logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Often violent / loud emotional outbursts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sudden loudness or physical escalation as a punctuation point to release built-up tension. These outbursts should feel like a logical culmination of the character's commitment. Avoid gratuitous physical harm or shock for its own sake; ensure it serves the comedic escalation.
